subject: Architecture
title: Willis Tower: Bundled Tube Genius
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Willis Tower: Bundled Tube Genius.

hook.text: Chicago's Willis Tower (formerly Sears Tower) used nine tubes bundled together like a pack of cigarettes.

buildup.text: Engineer Fazlur Khan realized bundling tubes let each one stop at different heights, reducing wind load.

discovery.text: The staggered tubes create the tower's distinctive stepped profile — engineering dictated the design.

twist.text: The Skydeck's glass ledge lets visitors stand 1,353 feet above the ground on a transparent floor.

climax.text: The bundled tube concept influenced every supertall tower built afterward, from Taipei 101 to the Burj.

punchline.text: Nine small tubes, bundled together, beat one big one.

quiz.question: What is the 'bundled tube' system used in the Willis Tower?
options: Nine structural tubes grouped together, stopping at different heights
A single hollow concrete tube reinforced with steel cables
Multiple elevator shafts bundled in the center of the building

details.summary: Willis Tower (formerly Sears Tower) in Chicago, completed in 1973, introduced the bundled tube structure — nine square tubes of varying heights bundled together like a cluster of boxes. This approach created a stepped profile that reduced wind load while maximizing usable floor space.
details.whyItMatters: Engineer Fazlur Khan's bundled tube was a breakthrough that made extreme height efficient. The concept influenced supertall design globally and kept Willis Tower as the world's tallest building for 25 years.
takeaways: Completed in 1973 in Chicago with a bundled tube structure
Nine tubes of varying heights reduce wind loads efficiently
It was the world's tallest building for 25 years

faq.question: What is a bundled tube structure?
faq.answer: Nine independent square tubes are bundled together at the base, with some terminating at different heights as the building rises. This creates a stepped profile that reduces wind resistance at the top while providing maximum floor area at the lower levels where space is most valuable.

faq.question: Why was Willis Tower renamed from Sears Tower?
faq.answer: Sears, Roebuck and Company moved out in 1992. In 2009, the Willis Group, a London-based insurance broker, obtained naming rights as part of a lease agreement. Many Chicagoans still refer to it as the Sears Tower despite the official rename.
